step.description: a rule stored as a row: for each binding of `match`, write `write` with its variables filled. A step a workflow `contains` writes a case for the item and stamps `made` on what it creates

match.description: the query whose bindings it acts on: `$o .order, !shipped`, or several patterns joined by shared variables

write.description: the bundles it writes for each binding: a string `$name` the match bound is its value, and an entity eid `$name` it did not bind is a fresh entity, one per binding

when.description: `write` runs inside the write that made it match, `commit` (the default) after that write commits; a step carrying `wake` or `watch` runs when that fires instead

workflow.description: a structure of steps: it `contains` them, and which feeds which is computed from their matches and writes

workflow_case.description: a case: one item moving through a workflow, its eid derived from the workflow and the item so a rematch finds it. Named `case` once two packages may declare one label (@yaks/trial declares `case`)

for.description: the item: the entity the case's first step matched

made.description: which case and step wrote this row; a row made before its step's last edit reads as outdated

case.description: the case it was written for

step_due.description: one after-commit run a step owes, written in the transaction of the write that matched so a crash or restart never loses it; `step_run` runs it and deletes it in the same write

binding.description: the entities its match bound, in its patterns' order (`''` for one it left unbound); the run asks the match again anchored to them, so it acts on the present

by.description: who wrote the write that matched, whom the step's write is signed as

via.description: the session or client that write came in on

depth.description: how many after-commit step writes came before the one that matched: past 32, the chain is taken for a step whose output keeps matching it

step_run.description: run a step after the write that matched it commits, for the binding its `step_due` names, and delete the `step_due` in the same write

step_fire.description: run a step whose wake or watch fired, its match asked of the whole graph, written as the step's writer

step.description: a rule stored as a row: what it matches, what it writes for each binding, and when

workflow.description: steps it `contains`, and the cases moving through them
